# Starter: renamed course grade history

## Setup

```
npm install
npm test        # run the test suite (all tests currently fail -- the
                 # function is a stub)
npm run typecheck
```

## The task

`src/gradeHistory.ts` exports `getGradeHistoryForCourse(courseId)`, which is
supposed to return every grade distribution record on file for a course,
across that course's full history. Right now it's an unimplemented stub —
read the JSDoc contract above the function signature for exactly what it
needs to do.

Courses can be renamed or renumbered by the campus (subject changes, number
changes, or both) while remaining "the same course" — same internal `id`,
same enrollment history, same everything except the label. Grade
distribution records are historical: each one is stamped with whatever
subject+number was correct at the time it was recorded, and that stamp is
never rewritten after the fact.

This is the same problem from Round 1, now concrete: design and implement
whatever mechanism you need so that looking up a course's grade history
follows it across any number of renames, without accidentally pulling in an
unrelated course's records.

Look at `src/fixtures.ts`:
- `courses` — three courses. One has never been renamed. One was renamed
  once. One was renamed twice.
- `courseIdentityHistory` — every subject+number a course has ever held
  (current identity included), keyed by the course's stable internal `id`.
- `gradeDistributions` — raw grade records, each stamped with whatever
  subject+number was correct at the time.

## Task

Implement `getGradeHistoryForCourse` so that it returns a course's complete
grade history, correctly following it across any number of renames. Run
`npm test` — you should end with all tests passing, and you should not need
to modify the test file or the fixtures.

You have real latitude in *how* you build this (a lookup structure you build
inline, an index you precompute, whatever you'd actually want to ship) — the
tests only care about the output.

If you have extra time and want to think beyond what the tests check: what
happens if a subject+number gets "freed up" and later reused by a
*different, unrelated* course? `validFrom`/`validUntil` on
`CourseIdentity` exist for exactly this reason — think about whether/how
you'd use them. This isn't required to pass the suite, but come prepared to
talk about it.

## AI usage

You're welcome to use AI tools (Copilot, Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) for
this exercise — most engineers here do, day to day. Please keep a log of the
prompts you used (a plain text or markdown file is fine, doesn't need to be
formatted nicely) and bring it to the debrief. We're not scoring "did you use
AI," we're interested in how you used it: what you asked for, what you
accepted as-is, what you pushed back on or rewrote yourself.
